newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper rejects rebel demands on captives.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper rejects rebel demands on captives.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper on Monday ruled out further concessions in the process to secure the release of 60 soldiers taken prisoner by leftist rebels three months ago.

In a televised speech, Samper said he would honour his pledge to pull the army out of a 5,400-square-mile (14,000 sq km) swathe of jungle in southern Caqueta province for 10 days starting on Friday to make way for the troop handover.

But he rejected a call by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), issued over the weekend, to include the town of Remolinos del Caguan -- site of a newly built military base -- in the zone to be demilitarized.
"The government does not consider it possible, for security reasons, to clear troops from this area," Samper said.

The soldiers were captured, and 27 others were killed, on Aug. 30 when the FARC, the country's oldest and largest guerrilla army, overran a military post in neighbouring Putumayo province. The attack signalled the start of one of the bloodiest rebel offensives in three decades of armed uprising.

According to political analysts, Samper had a tough, behind-the-scenes fight with army commanders, humiliated by the original attack, to convince them to demilitarize any area at all for the handover of the captured soldiers. It is not likely he will convince the army chiefs to cave in to the FARC's latest demand, the analysts said.

But a FARC spokesman, in Mexico City, told Reuters: "It's not a question of 14,000 or 15,000 square kilometres. If the military do not clear Remolinos the FARC has no safe access into and out of the demilitarized zone."
The president is now pinning his hopes for the release of the soldiers on a seasonal show of goodwill by the FARC.
